name: Dysraphism-Cleft Lip/Palate-Limb Reduction Defects Syndrome
aliases: Dysraphism with Cleft Lip and Limb Reduction

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Dysraphism-Cleft Lip/Palate-Limb Reduction Defects Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of spinal dysraphism including spina bifida or myelomeningocele
Cleft lip and/or cleft palate confirmed by clinical examination
Congenital limb reduction defects such as absence or hypoplasia of digits or limbs
Evidence of neurodevelopmental delay or motor impairment
Radiological confirmation of spinal dysraphism and limb anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: spinal dysraphism, cleft lip/palate, and limb reduction defects
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by imaging studies; genetic testing may assist but is not definitive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Non-midline cleft of the upper lip

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biomarkers identified
imaging: MRI or ultrasound showing spinal dysraphism
X-ray or MRI demonstrating limb reduction defects
CT or MRI confirming cleft palate anatomy
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; possible sporadic or multifactorial etiology
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic triad of dysraphism, cleft lip/palate, and limb defects

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of spinal dysraphism and limb reduction defects
No associated cleft lip/palate or spinal dysraphism

redFlags: Open spinal defect with cerebrospinal fluid leakage
Severe feeding difficulties causing failure to thrive
references: Orphanet: Dysraphism-Cleft Lip/Palate-Limb Reduction Defects Syndrome, ORPHA:2476
Smith DW, et al. Dysraphism and associated anomalies: clinical features and management. J Pediatr. 1995.
Jones KL. Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation. 7th Edition. 2013.
